chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'When the woman says, "My husband is prohibited to me like the back of my mother," then there is no expiation upon her.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And a man from the Ansar, from the Banu Al-Najjar, came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, "I pronounced Zihar from my wife, then I had intercourse with her before I expiated."'

So he (peace be upon him) said: 'And what carried you to do that?' He said, 'When I pronounced Zihar, I saw the glitter of her anklet and the whiteness of her leg in the moonlight, so I had intercourse with her before I expiated.'
So he (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Alienate her until you expiate,' and he ordered him with one expiation and that he should seek forgiveness from Allah.

key_terms.بَنِي النَّجَّار: Banu Al-Najjar (a clan of the Ansar)
key_terms.ظَهَر: Zihar (likening wife's back to mother's back)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a man who pronounces Zihar and has intercourse with his wife before expiating?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudence of Zihar, specifically addressing the scenario where a man engages in intercourse before completing the expiation, ruling that only a single expiation is required rather than a double penalty. It also highlights the scholarly view that the obligation of expiation applies primarily to the husband, as the wife's pronouncement does not carry the same legal weight. This ruling underscores the balance between maintaining marital bonds and ensuring ritual purity through specific acts of worship.
